title: Keep the Beacon Lit
story:
NORA // 03:15 // ALERT. STATUS PAGE: DOWN. LAST HOST: OLD-SERVER. UPTIME RECORD: BROKEN.

The monitoring bot has been serving the station's status page from a server that now reboots every few hours. Each time it drops, the crew loses sight of the generators and the greenhouse heaters.

Give the page a new home. Start `nginx:alpine` as a container called `beacon`, and run it in the background. Ingrid wants the terminal back for the next job, and the beacon has to keep burning while you work.
objectives: The container must be running in the background (detached), not holding your terminal
startingState: Docker is installed and no containers exist. The `nginx:alpine` image is already downloaded.
hints: A container started normally is attached to your terminal and stops being useful the moment you press Ctrl+C. Docker can detach a container so it runs in the background.
Combine the detach flag `-d` with `--name` before the image: `docker run -d --name <name> <image>`. Check the result with `docker ps`.

```bash
docker run -d --name beacon nginx:alpine
docker ps
```

validation.description: The web server inside `beacon` answers on its own port 80

debrief: Detached mode (`-d`) starts the container's main process in the background and prints the container ID. Pro tip: `docker logs -f beacon` lets you watch a detached container without attaching to it.
